basis: Lysosomal storage; skeletal and neurologic dysfunction each common (~30%+ across major forms). Vision-threatening disease is subtype-dependent; ocular deposits may spare function.

decisions.ocular: none: visual loss is concentrated in ML IV and sialidosis; an umbrella frequency >=30% is not established, and corneal/cherry-red deposits alone do not establish damage.

basis: Hydrocephalus and scapular/costovertebral defects define syndrome; dental enamel defects occur in 30-79%. Pigmentation, photosensitivity and obesity do not establish additional organ injury.

decisions.dermatologic: none: pigmentation and photosensitivity occur in 30-79%, but persistent skin injury or loss of function is not demonstrated.
decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: obesity in 30-79% does not establish direct endocrine or metabolic dysfunction; obesity alone is a separately diagnosed condition.

basis: Pontocerebellar hypoplasia with motor-neuron/axonal disease; weakness and amyotrophy reflect denervation. Contractures in 1/3 do not demonstrate direct muscle or joint disease.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: amyotrophy and contractures (each 1/3) are secondary to neurologic dysfunction; intrinsic muscle or joint damage by the disease process is not established.

basis: Bardet-Biedl phenotype: retinal dystrophy, obesity/hypogonadism and renal disease are major criteria; cognitive impairment affects ~60%+. Polydactyly omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.renal: primary: renal developmental/parenchymal disease is a major Bardet-Biedl diagnostic criterion and an important feature of BBS12 disease.
decisions.neurologic: involved: developmental/cognitive impairment affects roughly 60% or more; retained under the cap because of substantial functional impairment.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: polydactyly qualifies as a major feature but is omitted at the four-axis cap in favor of visual, metabolic, renal and neurodevelopmental disease.

basis: Childhood neuromuscular GBE deficiency has characteristic skeletal myopathy and dilated cardiomyopathy from polyglucosan storage; hepatic and adult neurologic forms are distinct.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: dilated cardiomyopathy is a characteristic defining manifestation of childhood neuromuscular GSD IV alongside skeletal myopathy, although severity varies.

basis: Ocular, branchial skin and characteristic lip defects define BOFS; hearing impairment occurs in 5/6 and conductive loss in 80-99%. Renal anomalies are occasional (5-29%).

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: cleft/pseudocleft upper lip is part of the major characteristic facial criterion; tooth agenesis and microdontia additionally occur in 30-79%.

basis: Defining skin encasement, limb/muscle hypoplasia and severe oral defects; microphthalmia 2/2. Cardiac/renal defects (1/2) omitted at cap; CNS cysts/lung lobation lack proven functional injury.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: severe oral malformation and omphalocele are defining developmental defects, each reported in 2/2 patients.
decisions.neurologic: none: intracranial cysts occur in 2/2, but functional impact is unclear; four systems with clearer tissue defects fill the cap.
decisions.ocular: involved: microphthalmia in 2/2 directly impairs eye development; the three primary slots prioritize defining skin, limb/muscle and severe oral defects.

basis: Abdominal-wall closure defect defined by bowel herniation into an umbilical sac; the wall defect and displaced intestine are primary locations.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: bowel herniation into the umbilical sac defines omphalocele; additional intrinsic intestinal injury is not required for a primary location label.

basis: Eye dermoids/skin aplasia define OES; CNS malformations 80-99%, bowel aganglionosis 30-79%. Cap omits hearing, renal, cardiac, laryngeal and skeletal defects.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: aganglionic megacolon is reported in 30-79% and directly impairs intestinal function; its severity supports retention under the cap.
decisions.otologic: none: hearing impairment qualifies at 30-79%, but the four-axis cap prioritizes similarly frequent, more severe aganglionic bowel disease.

basis: Developmental disability, seizures and delayed myelination define CNS disease; common strabismus alone does not demonstrate direct eye damage or visual loss.

decisions.ocular: none: common strabismus alone does not establish direct ocular damage or visual loss; it can reflect impaired central control of eye alignment.
